name: Four levels of loop-to-story arrangement: (1) subtractive Lego-block arrangement from a duplicated loop shaped by an energy contour, (2) turnaround-and-marker transitions at section edges, (3) a performed protagonist element that crescendos and decrescendos across sections, (4) an additive cinematic pass that starts from silence and adds only motivated elements
goal: Turn a 16-bar loop into a musical story in four escalating levels. Level 1 (subtractive): duplicate the loop across the whole target length (4-5 minutes), then cut away in 8- or 16-bar blocks following an energy contour (low start, build to the middle, kick-out dips, peak, outro); add a little silence at the start and room at the end for reverb tails. Level 2 (transitions): at each section edge add a turnaround (signals the end: remove low energy, reverse reverb swell or noise riser) and a marker on the downbeat (a splash: white noise, crash, one percussion hit into big reverb, stutter or false drop), built from the track's own timbres resampled, reversed or processed; transitions can be explicit or hypnotic. Level 3 (performance): record a performed element (e.g. filter, level or intensity moves on one sound) that starts mellow, grows to dominant and subsides, spanning section boundaries as the 'protagonist'; split and move the audio if needed. Level 4 (additive): start from silence and add elements only when the music is motivated (when you would get bored), like a film composer, letting well-designed elements play for a long time.

source.title: turn your loop into a story: an arrangement masterclass
source.transcript_note: Auto-generated YouTube Show transcript; values are as spoken and approximate where the speaker says 'about' or 'around'.

prerequisites: A DAW with duplicate-time, insert-time and split commands
A finished loop (16 bars in the video)
A controller or automation for performing one element (optional)

outputs.name: arrangement
outputs.description: Section-based arrangement with transitions and a performed protagonist element

outputs.name: energy_contour
outputs.description: Sketch of the intended energy curve over time

constraints: Original synthesis recipe; not affiliated with any vendor named in the source. Recreate in browser/Web Audio (Polyrhythm Studio) or any hybrid synth with comparable modules; no presets, banks or samples copied.
DAW shortcuts in the video are product-specific; use the equivalent duplicate-time / insert-silence / split commands in Ableton or any DAW.
For Matt's ambient/cinematic system the additive level 4 is the target; levels 1-3 are scaffolding. Keep drums entering early and steady even in the additive pass if the piece has a beat.
Performed elements should move musically and gradually so split/moved takes still join cleanly.

steps.action: Decide the target length; select the loop and duplicate it end to end until the timeline exceeds that length; trim any extra.
steps.expect: A 'block of clay' filling the whole song length.

steps.action: Sketch an energy contour: low start, additions toward the middle, dips where the kick goes away, a maximum, then an outro. Optionally align a reference track to the grid and copy its arrangement (not its sounds).
steps.expect: An energy plan to subtract against.

steps.action: Subtract in 8- or 16-bar blocks so each section boundary adds some elements and removes others. Insert a little silence at the start and leave space at the end for reverb tails.
At each section edge, add a turnaround in the last bar(s): remove low-end energy and add a reverse reverb swell or noise riser built from the track's own sounds.
steps.expect: The listener senses a new section coming.

steps.action: On the new section's downbeat, add a marker: white noise burst, crash, one percussion hit into a big reverb, a stutter, or a false drop (withhold the first hit).
steps.expect: A clear splash of energy at the boundary.

steps.action: Revisit breaks and drops: e.g. a very sparse moment, then build, build, build, then a short silence before the drop.

Pick one protagonist element and perform it across the whole track (record filter/level/intensity moves) so it starts mellow, grows dominant and subsides, crossing section boundaries; split and rearrange the performance if needed.
steps.expect: A storyline that glues sections together; energy feels gradual and linear rather than A/B blocky.

steps.action: Additive pass: from silence, peel everything back to almost nothing and add elements one at a time only when the music needs them (when you notice boredom), giving each element time and space.
steps.expect: A sparse, cinematic arrangement where every entry is motivated.

verification: Each section boundary has a turnaround before it and a marker on it (or is deliberately seamless).
One element's level or intensity curve rises then falls across at least three sections.
The track starts from silence or near-silence and ends with space for tails.
